source.title: Open problems: Lieb-Thirring type inequalities for Schrödinger operators with a complex-valued potential.

accepted.question_text: Let H = -Δ + V be a Schrödinger operator on R^d, where the potential V is complex-valued and belongs to L^p(R^d) with p ≥ 1 when d = 1, p > 1 when d = 2, and p ≥ d/2 when d ≥ 3. For real-valued V, the classical Lieb-Thirring inequality bounds the discrete spectrum by Σ_{λ ∈ σ_d(H)} |λ|^{p-d/2} ≤ C(p,d) ||V||_{L^p}^p, where C(p,d) depends only on p and d. Is there an analogous bound for complex-valued potentials stating that Σ_{λ ∈ σ_d(H)} dist(λ,[0,∞))^p / |λ|^{d/2} ≤ C(p,d) ||V||_{L^p}^p, where the sum runs over the discrete spectrum σ_d(H) and dist(λ,[0,∞)) denotes the distance from λ to the nonnegative real axis?
accepted.context_brief: Lieb-Thirring inequality for complex-valued Schrödinger potentials

evidence.quote: The Lieb-Thirring inequality states that, if H=-Δ +V, V ∈ L^{p}(R^{d};R), p≥ 1 if d=1, p>1 if d=2 and p ≥ d/2 if d ≥3, then [sum formula omitted here in the review context] where C(p,d) depends only on p and on d. The authors raise the following question: is it true that, if V is complex valued, then the inequality [ Σ_{λ ∈ σ_d(H)} dist(λ,[0,∞))^{p} / |λ|^{d/2} ≤ C(p,d) ||V||_{L^{p}}^{p} ] holds? They review several results which may be considered weakened versions of (1).
